text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Streaming p99 latency SLO breach on pool-gamma (p95=420ms, p99=2.9s) — auto-root cause candidates triggered: multi-tenant IO pressure, KV-cache evictions. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/streams/pool-gamma

eva-sre: saw the alert, paging @sana-oncall. Is pool-gamma the shared nvme-backed cluster?

sana-oncall: yes, that's the shared GPU pool with local NVMe. I'm pulling metrics now. Oncall handoff: I'm oncall until 18:00 UTC, I'll take lead.

matt-ml: customers reported streaming stalls and chunked responses, some clients saw websocket stalls + reconnects. Noticed model kv-cache miss rate jumped ~40%.

neil-platform: checking host-level IO — I see a burst of writeback/flush activity starting ~3342099800. Likely a tenant doing heavy checkpoint or checkpoint+upload.

eva-sre: can we identify noisy tenant? Top IO pids?

neil-platform: already grabbed iostat and blktrace snippets. Quick grep shows spike from node gnode-17, docker id 94f3 (tenant-691). iostat -x snapshot:
```
Device            r/s     w/s    rkB/s   wkB/s   rrqm/s  wrqm/s  avgrq-sz  await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         10.00  480.00  100.00 120000.0    0.00    0.00    250.00    12.4   0.30  95.0
```

sana-oncall: 95% util, that's bad. Any process level IO stats?

neil-platform: blkparse and pidstat point to a java checkpoint job kicked at 3342099755 under tenant-691. It flushed ~110GB in ~30s.

matt-ml: that aligns with the timing of p99 spikes + streaming stalls. When NVMe is saturated, GPU DMA stalls on certain ops (we've seen before).

eva-sre: immediate action: can we throttle tenant-691 IO or move them to a ded pool?

neil-platform: options: 1) Apply blkio cgroup weight tweak to reduce IO priority for that container; 2) Evacuate tenant to dedicated node; 3) Apply temporary tc qdisc on nvme device (messy). I'd prefer cgroup weight first.

sana-oncall: do it. Command to run?

neil-platform: running (on gnode-17):
```bash
# find cgroup path for container
cgpath=$(grep -l "94f3" /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/*/cgroup.procs | sed 's|/cgroup.procs||')
echo $cgpath
cgset -r blkio.weight=10 "$cgpath" || echo 'fallback: echo 10 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/$cgpath/blkio.weight'
```

eva-sre: applying now.

eva-sre: applied weight=10 for tenant-691 on gnode-17, pinging metrics.

incident-bot: NOTE: mitigation applied by eva-sre (blkio.weight=10) at 3342100018. Update: p99 dropping from 2.9s -> 650ms within two minutes.

matt-ml: kv-cache miss rate still elevated but latency improving. We might need a second action to reduce GPU stalls: disable aggressive prefetch/batching for tenant-691's model streams to reduce bursty IO.

sana-oncall: can ML adjust at inference layer? Matt?

matt-ml: yes. Pushing a dynamic config change to reduce streaming concurrency for tenant-691 to 2 (from 8). Will roll canary to the node first.

matt-ml: pushing patch:
```json
{"route":"/inference/tenant-691/*","streaming.concurrency":2,"batching.max_batch_size":4}
```

matt-ml: deployed canary to gnode-17. Monitoring.

neil-platform: host-level metrics show write utilization dropped to 48% after blkio change and app-level concurrency drop. p99 now ~420ms, p95 ~180ms.

lia-cs: lia-cs (from support): customers AppX and Brightdocs reported increased timeouts. Any ETA to full remediation or customer impact summary?

sana-oncall: immediate mitigation reduced SLO breach. We'll keep tenant-691 IO throttled and run an evacuation if they need long checkpoint windows. Short term: assigned incident priority P1 -> now P2 since partial mitigation reduced customer impact.

eva-sre: action items while incident is active:
- Keep blkio.weight enforced until tenant schedules checkpoint during maintenance window
- Schedule evacuation of tenant-691 to reserved pool (dedicated-gamma) if they have >50GB flush within 24h
- Add a blocking rule to the scheduler to avoid colocating heavy nvme checkpoint workloads with streaming pools
- Postmortem: triage root cause and recommend tenant-side backpressure for checkpoint flushes

matt-ml: also suggested longer term: introduce KV-cache writeback smoothing (drip checkpointing) and add per-tenant streaming concurrency quotas enforced at router.

neil-platform: I'll file a repro ticket with steps to reproduce the nvme saturation and attach blktrace. Also will open a change to add default blkio.weight=500 for streaming pool containers to avoid single-tenant stomping.

lia-cs: noting affected customers for the post-incident report: AppX (15% timeouts), Brightdocs (7% reconnects), internal-sandbox (noisy dev workload flagged). Lia will coordinate outreach.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied, partial recovery — SLO now green for pool-gamma (p99 < target). Incident -> monitoring state.

sana-oncall: assigning follow-ups: @neil-platform to schedule evacuation + config change, @matt-ml to implement concurrency quotas, @eva-sre to write initial timeline and notify oncall rotation.

neil-platform: started evacuation runbook for tenant-691 -> creating ticket INF-7892 and scheduling migration to ded pool during low-traffic window.

neil-platform: logs/timestamped traces uploaded: https://internal.redwood/trace/INF-7892

neil-platform: proposed kernel-level changes for long term: enable blkio.weight v2 migrations and tune writeback parameters.

matt-ml: will add tests to eval harness to simulate checkpoint+streaming interference.

eva-sre: thanks everyone — I'll start the incident timeline and draft a short CS note. If anyone sees p99 creep again, @sana-oncall is primary.

lia-cs: thanks, patching support notes and will be ready to escalate if customers need a dedicated credit or SLA remediation.

sana-oncall: closing coordination thread for now — marking incident as mitigated. Will reopen if metrics regress. :white_check_mark:
